To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the coefficient of variation in response time over views can be used to measure learning, and (2) practice effects can be divided into two components: a task learning component that is independent of object representation, and an object learning component that is specific to individual objects and that is related to the development of canonical object views

the learning of object recognition is object-specific, not task-specific, and that this object-specific learning is reflected in changes in the distribution of response time over different views of an object, not in the mean response time.
the coefficient of variation is a sensitive measure of learning and that practice with computer-generated amoebas leads to the development of canonical object views.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of object recognition and its relation to the nature of the representation of objects.
the nature of learning in visual object recognition.
the development of a computational theory of visual learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the human observer's ability to recognize an object improves with practice.
task and object learning in visual recognition can be separated.
the process of learning to recognize objects is not only one of improving the ability to recognize the same object under different viewing conditions, but also one of learning the object's structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
practice with objects results in learning that is specific to those objects and that can be described by changes in the representations used in recognition.
the process of learning is not only a function of task and stimulus, but also the nature of the response measure.
the process of recognition is a complex one, in which a number of factors interact to produce a variety of effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, with the appropriate response measure, the study of human learning in recognition can provide insight into the nature of the representation used in recognition.
the use of response time measures can help to distinguish between task and object learning in visual recognition.
the study of human performance in object recognition can reveal properties of the process that would otherwise be difficult to access.
